action: opened the order: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.
Untapped capability: proposed Tap, Duel, Tail
person at the terminal: proposed Contents (contents-widget), Salvage (salvage-widget), Not You (outage-widget)
Delight: proposed Reflex (reflex-widget), Deja Vu (dejavu-widget), Kudos (kudos-widget)
took the order at ideation

stamped reject on "Duel": Two full subagent runs, two worktrees and a diff applied to the working tree is a workflow, not a card: the cost and the failure modes (background agents that cannot answer permission prompts, a dirty tree at take) are out of proportion, and the Agent tool already runs isolated worktree agents on request.

stamped reject on "Salvage": Claude Code already keeps a cleared draft in prompt history and has a stash, so what is left is crash recovery, paid for by writing everything the person types to a plain-text file.
stamped reject on "Not You": A status-page lookup that fires a few times a year and hangs on one hard-coded outside endpoint; a person opens the page once and does not mention the card.

stamped reject on "Reflex": The answer time is derived by subtraction from classic.PermissionRequest timing the types do not promise and breaks when dialogs queue, the verdict rests on an assumed reading pace, and it is a second reading of the guard-widget and stakes-widget dialog family.

stamped reject on "Deja Vu": A word-overlap match over saved sessions is a guess that stays silent for most people, and it sits in the insight, resume and ledger family that already reads the same history.

stamped reject on "Kudos": The sentence is a model's opinion that git blame can locate but not verify, delivered through one more Claude-written tool like notebook, wishlist and board, for 80 to 100 tokens of context every session.

stamped reject on "Tail": Not chosen: it works with process.spawn, but the engine's own background shell already keeps a dev server and lets Claude read its output, deciding what counts as an error is a word heuristic, and killing a dev server's child tree on Windows is unsolved; Tap opens a wider door.

stamped reject on "Contents": Not chosen: ui.scroll exists, but the ids of prompt and reply rows are unproven for a card to collect, it works in fullscreen only, and Margin (WO-0016) is already the transcript-interaction widget in flight.
named the widget tap-widget ("Tap")
stamped pass: Tap is the only idea that opens a capability no widget and no engine feature has: any connected MCP server as a live card for zero tokens, through $.mcp.call, which exists as claimed.
